v1_observation: The frozen V1 catalog contains 309 pre-existing specifications and the pre-V2 package surface.
v2_decision: During shadow implementation the worktree also contains ratified V2 analysis, repository, and specification-compiler modules; the V1 oracle projects them out while requiring every frozen entry and derived transport to remain byte-identical.
rationale: The additional inputs are independently specified and verified but are not V1 parity subjects or V2 authority before Gate 5; excluding only their named prefixes and exports preserves the frozen causal comparison without hiding changes to any pre-existing input.

v1_observation: V1 includes architecture.md in the normative specRevision, so a rationale-only edit invalidates the specification as if behavior changed.
v2_decision: V2 keeps architecture and history in context or presentation revisions while SpecificationSnapshot identity includes only normative resources and static diagnostics.
rationale: Rationale must remain visible but cannot become behavioral authority; the full corpus retains every authored contract field and a focused regression proves rationale-only edits preserve normative identity.

v1_observation: V1 deduplicates a logical dependency but retains only the first traversal occurrence, so the edge ID and diagnostic evidence can change when compiler or export traversal order changes.
v2_decision: V2 derives the logical edge ID from the relationship tuple and retains every contributing occurrence in a canonically ordered evidence collection.
rationale: Traversal order is not semantic authority; complete occurrence evidence gives stable graph identity without hiding the exact V1 representative during parity qualification.

v1_observation: V1 standard-library declaration identities embed compiler-bundle file offsets, so the same Date symbol changes identity across TypeScript revisions.
v2_decision: V2 identifies a standard-library symbol by the TypeScript platform provider and qualified symbol path, independent of bundled file layout and byte positions.
rationale: Compiler packaging is not semantic identity; stable platform coordinates preserve the same logical target across qualified upgrades without leaking an absolute or revision-local location.

v1_observation: V1 exposes Node-checker reduction details such as boolean literal unions, distributed intersections, flattened authored aliases, and compiler-expanded non-exported closure declarations as the declaration wire shape.
v2_decision: V2 retains authored alias and algebraic provenance with checker-resolved targets and substitutions; checker-reduced views are separate derived capabilities, while non-exported issue-free closure additions or removals are enumerated rather than silently normalized.
rationale: The representations denote the same TypeScript contract, while the V2 base is attributable, stable across compiler reductions, and more useful to indexing and policy consumers. Exported coverage and shared identity/kind remain exact, fixture-proven equivalence classes are reported, and unknown differences still fail.

v1_observation: V1 omits declarations that are checker-reachable from exported APIs and therefore omits their external API dependency relationships, including declarations whose detailed type representation is explicitly partial.
v2_decision: V2 walks the complete exported declaration closure and retains an API relationship for each reachable external owner; parity accepts an additional relationship only when the source module fact proves declaration existence and reachability from an export.
rationale: A representation issue describes completeness of normalized type shape, not uncertainty about a separately Checker-resolved symbol owner. The fail-closed reachability predicate still rejects implementation dependencies while reporting every corrected relationship explicitly.

v1_observation: Node TypeScript reports exactly three TS7022 and TS7024 circular-inference diagnostics for the delayed Admin repository-factory closure, although the annotated public factory contract is sound and TypeScript-Go resolves the same project without diagnostics.
v2_decision: The qualified TypeScript-Go compiler is diagnostic authority in V2; parity records and accepts only the exact frozen module, codes, and locations instead of synthesizing obsolete Node compiler diagnostics.
rationale: Compiler-generation limitations are evidence, not product semantics. Any additional, moved, or changed diagnostic still fails, and the production-native cold and incremental fixture must remain diagnostic-free.

v1_observation: V1 embeds declaration byte offsets in every public workspace and package symbol identity, so inserting unrelated text before a declaration renames it and every referencing graph fact.
v2_decision: V2 identifies public declarations by portable source coordinates and qualified authored symbol paths; source spans remain provenance and parity canonicalizes only the positional V1 form of the same symbol.
rationale: Byte offsets are locations, not semantic identity. Stable logical IDs are required for incremental materialization, while lexical qualification prevents same-spelled nested declarations from collapsing.

v1_observation: V1 stops package ownership discovery at a valid nested package.json without a name, classifying files such as zod/v4/core and hono/dist/types as unowned pnpm-store paths.
v2_decision: V2 treats nameless nested manifests as module-format metadata and continues to the nearest named package owner; parity rewrites only an unowned physical target whose portable target file already proves that package.
rationale: Physical package-manager layout is not module ownership. The normalization is narrow, requires an existing package source coordinate, and leaves genuinely unowned sources failing.

v1_observation: V1 and TypeScript-Go can select different declaration entry files inside the same external package even when the resolved owner and import occurrence are identical.
v2_decision: V2 retains the exact TypeScript-Go provider file; parity accepts only a unique package-owned pair with exact source, owner, kind, specifier, flags, and location and enumerates both files.
rationale: The qualified compiler output is evidence and must not be rewritten to imitate another compiler generation; the pairing predicate rejects ambiguous or cross-package differences.

v1_observation: V1 often anchors a surface issue at the containing declaration and uses positional declaration IDs without retaining the observed unsupported display value.
v2_decision: V2 retains the exact native type-node column, stable declaration join, and observed value while semantic parity keeps code, message, source, and line exact.
rationale: Precise diagnostic provenance is more useful and truthful than a coarser compatibility location; every enriched issue remains enumerated and consumer output uses the unmodified V2 fact.

v1_observation: V1 emits unsupported issues for a frozen set of primitive, object, symbol, index-signature-composition, and compatible declaration-merge shapes that its normalizer cannot prove.
v2_decision: V2 emits lossless source-semantic facts for those exact declarations and does not synthesize obsolete unsupported issues; parity requires a frozen match, retained declaration, no V2-only issue, and enumerated removal.
rationale: Unsupported is an epistemic result, not a compatibility decoration. Reproducing a known false positive would make policies less sound; broad missing-issue acceptance remains forbidden.

v1_observation: For one frozen TS2345 diagnostic V1 flattens a Node-checker child message into the message string, while ttsc 0.26.2 exposes only the identical TypeScript-Go root message through its public driver diagnostic.
v2_decision: V2 retains the qualified ttsc root message and exact code and span; parity accepts only this one exact child-chain omission and records both messages as an upstream seam limitation.
rationale: Recomputing diagnostics through a second internal compiler path would duplicate ttsc filtering and preamble behavior. The root diagnostic remains authoritative and any additional message difference fails while a structured message-chain seam is pursued upstream.

v1_observation: V1 reports some uniquely bound generic parameters as unsupported types, including parameters owned by nested interface methods, conditional aliases, and generic callable returns.
v2_decision: V2 retains one exact lexical scope and index for each uniquely bound authored parameter and omits only the exact enumerated V1 false positives when the retained declaration proves both the binding and a matching parameter reference.
rationale: A generic constraint is not the parameter value, and reproducing the V1 warning would discard valid authored semantics. Ambiguous names and genuinely unbound infer parameters remain explicitly unsupported.

v1_observation: The frozen V1 catalog contains 34 nested Shell specifications for which verification emitted no row after assigning one workspace-dependency blocker only to the Shell root.
v2_decision: V2 joins catalog presence separately from evidence availability and emits a complete qualification for every authored Shell specification; the exact 21 pass and 13 error results, diagnostics, and coverage remain content-addressed evidence.
rationale: A missing V1 row is not a passing result or a new V2 module. Per-module evidence exposes the underlying problems without multiplying one causal blocker or erasing the other authored contracts.

v1_observation: V1 coverage totals mix blocked authored obligations, observation-target rules, and an incomplete dependency closure, so equal semantic outcomes can have traversal- and availability-dependent counts.
v2_decision: V2 counts evaluated authored obligations forward and normalized observed facts inverse; blocked downstream profiles count no fabricated obligations, structure target presence is one forward obligation, and the complete portable dependency closure remains visible.
rationale: The directions now have stable reusable meaning and cannot hide unmatched evidence in each other. All 368 changed coverage payloads are pinned and reviewed independently of status and diagnostic acceptance.

v1_observation: For six authored authentication leaves without implementation targets, V1 emits one MODULE_TARGET_MISSING rule for every surface and dependency obligation and counts all of them as unmatched coverage.
v2_decision: V2 reports the structure absence once and blocks the two dependent profiles with causal MODULE_TARGET_UNAVAILABLE evidence and zero fabricated coverage obligations.
rationale: Both systems remain indeterminate, but V2 preserves the capability DAG cause and avoids presenting unavailable evidence as dozens of proven mismatches. The exact 12 profile diagnostic payloads are pinned.

v1_observation: V1 emits exact false findings for compiler-generation limits, positional or reduced type identities, incomplete public closure, callable aliases treated as values, and imports marked stale after a required surface slot becomes unavailable.
v2_decision: V2 removes only the 43 content-addressed status or diagnostic differences justified by accepted semantic revisions and the invoked-signature, exact-alias, closure, and causal-dependency regressions in V2-REV-009.
rationale: Reproducing these findings would weaken the V2 contract. Any added finding, removed witness, changed count, or unmatched diagnostic remains unexplained drift; genuine remaining Kernel findings are not normalized away.

v1_observation: Eight V1 failing surface profiles diagnose a less precise public-type, ambiguity, heritage, member, or generic mismatch while omitting the exact mismatch or readonly obligation now available to V2.
v2_decision: V2 retains failure and replaces only those exact diagnostic multisets with identity-aware type, member, or readonly diagnostics grounded in the same authored and observed surfaces.
rationale: The finding is not suppressed; its causal code and count become more precise. The eight complete before-and-after multisets are content-addressed, and any additional diagnostic change fails.

v1_observation: Four V1 surface profiles aggregate to error because analyzer ambiguity or unsupported-shape diagnostics coexist with proven contract mismatches.
v2_decision: V2 resolves the unsupported evidence, retains the remaining proven mismatches, and therefore reports fail rather than error for the same four modules.
rationale: Error means the evaluator could not establish a judgment; fail means it did. Keeping error after exact evidence becomes available would misstate epistemic status, while the remaining failures and exact transition set stay visible.

v1_observation: V1 injects dependency occurrences from external unowned package files into governed modules' inbound lists even though no governed source module owns those edges and no module has the corresponding outbound relationship.
v2_decision: V2 inbound relationships are the inverse projection of governed module facts only; parity excludes and enumerates an external edge only when its source is unowned, absent from the governed module set, and attributable to a portable package coordinate.
rationale: A directed module graph cannot contain a relationship whose source vertex is outside its vertex set. Retaining these V1 edges would make inbound and outbound queries disagree and leak checkout paths; genuinely governed or non-package missing edges still fail.

v1_observation: The frozen V1 oracle contains 309 repository specifications, including Admin, Shell, Issues, and Events contracts that are no longer owned by the Kernel repository.
v2_decision: V2 derives its authoritative corpus from current authored specification sources, retains the immutable historical oracle, and projects that witness onto the exact discovered Kernel source set before comparison.
rationale: The active Kernel branch physically removes downstream application specifications. Preserving them as hidden parity inputs would make deleted ownership authoritative, while hard-coded domain excludes would overfit the repository. The generic source-identity projection keeps every retained Kernel row fail-closed and reports both excluded and newly absent source sets.

v1_observation: The frozen current-Kernel V1 coverage projections mix blocked authored obligations, observation-target rules, and an incomplete dependency closure in 223 exact profile differences.
v2_decision: V2 counts evaluated authored obligations forward and normalized observed facts inverse; blocked profiles count no fabricated obligations, structure target presence is one forward obligation, and complete portable dependency closure remains visible.
rationale: The 223 content-addressed witnesses are an exact subset of the previously audited 368; the other 145 belonged only to deleted downstream application specifications. Any changed or added current witness fails.

v1_observation: The current Kernel V1 oracle retains 20 false status or diagnostic findings caused by positional or reduced identities, incomplete public closure, callable aliases treated as values, and causal dependency bookkeeping.
v2_decision: V2 removes only those 20 content-addressed findings under the existing semantic regressions and accepted corrections.
rationale: The 20 witnesses are an exact subset of the prior 43; every removed witness belonged to a deleted downstream application specification. Newly removed, added, or changed current findings remain unexplained.

v1_observation: Five current Kernel V1 failing surface profiles diagnose a less precise public-type, ambiguity, heritage, member, or generic mismatch while omitting the exact mismatch or readonly obligation available to V2.
v2_decision: V2 retains failure and replaces only those five exact diagnostic multisets with identity-aware diagnostics grounded in the same authored and observed surfaces.
rationale: The five complete before-and-after multisets are an exact subset of the previously audited eight; no current finding is suppressed, and any additional refinement fails.

v1_observation: Two current Kernel V1 surface profiles aggregate to error because analyzer ambiguity or unsupported-shape diagnostics coexist with proven contract mismatches.
v2_decision: V2 resolves the unsupported evidence, retains the proven mismatches, and reports fail for those same two modules.
rationale: Error means judgment was unavailable while fail means it was established. The two transitions are an exact subset of the prior four and any changed current transition fails.
